title: Casper and the Echo
premise: Juniper Halloran has spent nine years alone on Kepler Station, tending a seed vault garden and maintaining a beacon whose original commission records were erased. When a distress signal arrives in Old Meridian—a language extinct since the Fleet's founding wars—she traces it to a colony ship the fleet officially declared never launched. The signal is a confession: the fleet's ruling council caused the disaster and buried it, and the truce keeping the colonies from civil war expires in forty days. Juniper must carry the recording to the relay at the edge of dead space, pursued by a council enforcer who was once her lover, while deciding whether truth is worth shattering a fragile peace. She reaches the relay, broadcasts the confession to every colony at once, and in doing so forces the fleet into open reckoning rather than quiet war—losing her invisibility forever but gaining a community of survivors who finally claim their own history.
about_author: J. M. Thornbury is the pen name of a former orbital agriculture engineer who spent six years on remote habitat stations before turning to fiction. Their work explores isolation, institutional memory, and the small acts of maintenance that hold civilizations together.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Establishes her solitary routine aboard Kepler Station: pruning gene-stabilized orchards, logging beacon pings no one answers, talking to seedlings meant for colonists two generations away. Emotional beat: contentment shadowed by loneliness; she has made peace with being forgotten, almost.

chapters.title: A Language with No Speakers
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The beacon catches a repeating distress signal in Old Meridian, which she recognizes only because her grandmother sang lullabies in it. Decoding fragments reveals coordinates in dead space and one word: 'witness.' Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as she realizes someone out there knows she exists.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She searches station archives for the beacon's commissioning order and finds the file surgically deleted—metadata showing erasure by fleet-level authority. First hint that her posting was never routine. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under nine years of assumed purpose.

chapters.title: The Visitor
chapters.summary: Enforcer Dae Okonkwo's POV. A council cutter docks unannounced; Dae arrives claiming routine inspection, but his questions about signal traffic are anything but routine. He and Juniper share history neither names. Emotional beat: tension between old intimacy and new suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Vault Remembers
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Distrusting Dae, Juniper hides a copy of the decoded signal inside the seed vault's climate-control lattice. He nearly catches her; their charged conversation reveals he suspects more than he admits. Emotional beat: loyalty tested before it's even declared.

chapters.title: Departure Without Permission
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Dae departs, leaving a veiled warning: report nothing, transmit nothing. Instead, Juniper burns her crops' growing cycle to fake a station failure and slips away on the maintenance skiff toward dead space. Emotional beat: grief and exhilaration—the gardener uprooting herself.

chapters.title: Dead Space Navigation
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Weeks alone in the silent zone where relays died in the founding wars; she repairs an ancient buoy to triangulate the signal's origin. Flashbacks reveal her grandmother was Old Meridian-born, a refugee of something unnamed. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening resolve.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Launched
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She finds the Meridian Star adrift, hull intact, life support cold. Inside: desiccated bodies, sealed logs, and evidence the ship was sabotaged after launch—not lost. Emotional beat: horror transmuting into righteous anger.

chapters.title: Confession in Extinct Tongue
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The ship's final log, voiced by its captain, recounts the council's decision to scuttle the colony rather than let it secede—and the cover-up that founded the current truce. Emotional beat: the weight of testimony carried across two centuries.

chapters.title: Pursuit Vector
chapters.summary: Dae's POV. The council orders Dae to intercept and silence Juniper; refusal means his family loses protection. He requests the assignment himself, telling himself he'll find another way. Emotional beat: self-deception fraying at the edges.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Dae boards Juniper's skiff mid-transit. Confrontation turns physical, then confessional: he knew about the Meridian Star years ago and stayed silent. She offers him the recording instead of a fight. Emotional beat: betrayal and tenderness colliding.

chapters.title: Forty Days
chapters.summary: Dae's POV. He falsifies his kill-report, buying Juniper time but painting himself into treason. Interludes show the council accelerating war preparations as the truce deadline nears. Emotional beat: the cost of a single act of mercy compounding.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She reaches the ancient relay hub, a cathedral of dead antennas, and discovers it still functions—but broadcasting requires authorization codes held by the council. Emotional beat: hope meeting a locked door.

chapters.title: Keys and Cages
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She spends days reverse-engineering the relay's authentication, living off emergency rations, haunted by the captain's voice. A council scout wing passes nearby; she goes dark for eighteen hours. Emotional beat: endurance as a form of defiance.

chapters.title: The Message Dae Carries
chapters.summary: Dae's POV. Ordered to destroy the relay, Dae arrives intending sabotage—but transmits the authorization codes to Juniper in the clear, sealing his fate. Emotional beat: loyalty finally choosing truth over institution.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. With hours before the truce expires, she patches the confession through every colonial channel simultaneously, adding her grandmother's lullaby as a signature the Old Meridian diaspora will recognize. Emotional beat: catharsis—the invisible woman making herself heard everywhere at once.

chapters.title: Fracture Lines
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Across the colonies, the broadcast detonates: protests, mutinies, council factions turning on each other. War seems certain until Old Meridian descendants occupy fleet arsenals without firing a shot. Emotional beat: chaos holding, barely, on the edge of violence.

chapters.title: The Council's Last Argument
chapters.summary: Dae's POV. Arrested, Dae faces the council and refuses to recant, forcing them to try him publicly—an admission the cover-up existed. His trial becomes the colonies' first shared hearing in generations. Emotional beat: dignity in defeat becoming leverage for change.

chapters.title: Ceasefire of Witnesses
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Summoned from hiding by survivors' descendants, Juniper testifies, presenting the seed vault manifest proving the fleet always intended to settle Meridian worlds—then abandoned them. The truce dissolves into negotiation instead of war. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly, arriving anyway.

chapters.title: Sentences
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The council is dissolved; some members flee, some face tribunals. Dae accepts exile to the Meridian Star's drift path as penance. Juniper declines every offered title, asking only for the station's deed. Emotional beat: accountability without vengeance.

chapters.title: Return to Kepler
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She comes home to find settlers have arrived in her absence, drawn by the broadcast, tending the garden badly and hopefully. She teaches them the pruning cycles and, for the first time, plants a row for people who will actually come. Emotional beat: solitude ending not with fanfare but with shared work.

chapters.title: The Echo Answers
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, coda. Years later, the beacon now carries traffic from a dozen rebuilt colonies. One night it returns a familiar pattern: the distress call, re-sent voluntarily by the Meridian Star's restored crew line—as remembrance, not plea. Juniper answers in Old Meridian: 'We hear you. We remember.' Emotional beat: grief transformed into continuity; the echo finally answered.
